sources.title: Hernán MA, Robins JM. Causal Inference: What If. Author-hosted updated 2026 PDF.
sources.locator: Chapter 16 §§16.1–16.6 and Technical Points 16.1–16.7; printed pp. 209–225, PDF pp. 218–234.

contents.name: Binary IV conditions, exclusion, joint exchangeability, and Wald estimand
contents.reason: Focused reading defines the three instrument conditions and the binary Wald functional; the carrier states the chosen joint-independence scope explicitly.

contents.name: Principal strata, monotonicity and complier average effect
contents.reason: §16.4 and Technical Point 16.7 define the four types and the LATE target; the local definition preserves the latent-subgroup qualification.

contents.name: Complier-share and complier-weighted reduced-form derivation
contents.reason: Technical Point 16.7 supports the decomposition route; the carrier supplies its complete local proof rather than relying on the source proof.

contents.name: Constant-effect/Wald interpretation
contents.reason: §16.3 and Technical Point 16.3 discuss homogeneity; the local theorem proves the stronger constant individual additive-effect case directly and does not import a structural-mean-model assumption.

contents.name: Weak-first-stage sensitivity and instrument limitations
contents.reason: §16.5 distinguishes a small population first stage from statistical weak-instrument diagnostics; the example is limited to ratio arithmetic and claims no sampling result.

contents.name: Randomized encouragement, defiers, and heterogeneous effects
contents.reason: The source motivates randomized encouragement and principal strata; the finite probability calculation is supplied and verified locally.

contents.name: Core IV assumptions do not by themselves identify the population ATE
contents.reason: Technical Point 16.2 discusses partial identification; the item gives a complete two-law finite counterexample with the exact IV conditions checked locally.

sources.title: Hyunseung Kang, Causal Inference: Identification Under Unmeasured Confounding (Instrumental Variables), University of Wisconsin–Madison lecture note.
sources.locator: Full HTML lecture: Randomized Encouragement Designs (counterfactuals and assumptions); Monotonicity-Based IV Assumptions; Compliance Types; Causal Estimand: LATE; Proof of Identification of the LATE. Estimation/inference and the later no-additive-interaction approach are not used.

contents.name: Potential treatments/outcomes, encouragement consistency, exclusion and instrument independence
contents.reason: The complete focused lecture units specify A(z), Y(a,z), randomized assignment and exclusion; the local carrier keeps all assumptions explicit.

contents.name: Compliance types and monotonicity partition
contents.reason: The source gives the four binary treatment-potential pairs; the carrier proves the exhaustive partition from binary values and monotonicity.

contents.name: Full LATE decomposition proof
contents.reason: The lecture supplied the proof route; the result is reproved locally with the stated integrability and positive-atom hypotheses.

contents.name: Randomized encouragement arithmetic and distinction from ATE
contents.reason: The local four-type model verifies the finite means and contrasts directly; the source example is context only.

contents.name: Defiers and effect heterogeneity limitations
contents.reason: The source explains why no-defiers is required; the supplied numerical population verifies the failure of the LATE ratio without that condition.

contents.name: Exclusion restriction and randomized assignment in the noncompliance model
contents.reason: §3.5.2 supports the assumption vocabulary; the pair follows the controlling plan's potential-outcome formulation.

contents.name: Limits of IV alone and observed-law implications
contents.reason: §§3.5.3–3.5.4 discuss bounds and instrumental inequalities; the local counterexample independently proves nonidentification of the ATE. Pearl §3.5 does not supply the monotonicity LATE proof.
